title: Backward implication for constructibility with integral coefficients
statement: theorem isConstructibleSheaf_integral_backward {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (hF : X.IsTorsionAbelianSheaf F) : let E := (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} ℤ) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).inv ⋙ ModuleCat.restrictScalars (ULift.ringEquiv : ULift.{u + 1} ℤ ≃+* ℤ).toRingHom IsConstructibleEtaleSheafOfSets ((sheafCompose X.smallEtaleTopology (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).obj F) → IsConstructibleSheaf ((sheafCompose X.smallEtaleTopology E).obj F)

source.place: Definition 03RW (definition-constructible), parts (2) and (3), and Lemma 095E (lemma-constructible-quasi-compact-quasi-separated); integral torsion specialization and underlying-set comparison written by Q1 for step 5 of lem-weil-pbc-curve-assertions-retract. Read the public Stacks pages for Tags 03RW and 095E.

proof.text: Keep the stratification supplied by set constructibility. On each stratum identify the set pullback with the underlying set sheaf of the abelian pullback. This comparison is proved in abelianSetPullbackIso: base change is representably flat, so its opposite left-Kan-extension indexing categories are filtered; forgetting abelian groups preserves those colimits and sheafification. Compose the left Kan extension and sheafification comparisons.

Transport the finite local set predicate across this isomorphism and apply finite_local_abelian_forget_iff. It supplies an abelian trivializing etale cover and finite abelian stalks at algebraically closed geometric points.

For any separably closed point lift it to an abelian trivializing cover member. The constant value on this member is finite: take its algebraic-closure residue-field point and identify the constant value with its finite abelian stalk. The stalk at the original separably closed point identifies with this same constant value. The Lean helpers abelianConstantStalkIso and finiteAbelianStalks prove these comparisons using the local-site equivalence, inverse-image stalk isomorphism, and constant-sheaf stalk isomorphism.

Apply the equivalence from abelian groups to integral modules to each constant restriction; equivalences preserve colimits and finite limits, so constant sheaves commute with this coefficient functor. Point.sheafFiberCompIso identifies its stalk with the coefficient functor applied to the finite abelian stalk. The counit of the integer-module equivalence preserves the finite underlying set, and a finite module is finitely generated (Module.Finite.of_finite and ModuleCat.isFinitelyGenerated_iff). This constructs both fields of IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf in integralFiniteLocal.

The coefficient equivalence commutes with the inverse image by the left Kan extension and sheafification comparisons, as proved in integralPullbackIso. Transport the finite locally constant module structure across this isomorphism and use the original stratification to construct IsConstructibleSheaf. No torsion hypothesis is used in this direction.
